40220104.text: Ah, that's Furina, right over there! She really is here all on her own...

40220108.text: Should I just give up? This is all... meaningless...

40220109.text: What was meant to happen did happen after all. Everyone's dead...

40220111.text: Give up, Furina. There's no point in holding out...

40220114.text: ...But what can I even do, other than to repeat meaningless apologies over and over...

40220117.text: Don't worry, Furina. It's just us...

40220118.text: Ahem... Heh... Ahahaha... So it is you, Blond Traveler from another land! Why, I almost thought you were someone from that mob of my ignorant subjects, come to kneel and beg for my forgiveness.

40220119.text: Furina... You were crying just now, weren't you? The tear stains on your face are obvious...

40220120.text: Uh... What do you mean, tear stains? Oh, I remember. The show at the opera house earlier this morning was so moving, I'm still trying to process it.

40220121.text: Hmph. Who did that uncivilized rabble think they were, disturbing my enjoyment of the arts?

40220122.text: They even dared to doubt their Archon... I must teach them a lesson. Hehe, I can just imagine their twisted and frustrated faces once they realize that I'm nowhere to be found...

40220123.text: Oh! And I'm sure Neuvillette and those people from the Marechaussee Phantom are freaking out right next to them, too. Hehehe...

40220902.text: *panting* Phew... I'm so tired... I totally thought they had caught me...

40220903.text: Ah, no, I mean, I nearly gave in to the sheer enthusiasm they displayed... Hahaha...

40220909.text: What's happening? The ground's shaking... Is it an earthquake?

40220910.text: Another disaster just struck, I suspect.

40220911.text: Yeah, a quake of this kind preceded the flooding in Poisson, didn't it?

40220912.text: It can't be... It's happening again...?

40220913.text: Well, there's no need to worry too much about that! Neuvillette's made some emergency plans, so the evacuation should go a lot smoother this time.

40220915.text: But the people of Poisson... They've already...

40220916.text: (Has Furina finally reached her limit? Now that she's talking about her actual feelings, she's starting to look far less stiff...)

40220917.text: You begin to talk amongst yourselves as Furina slowly calms down...

40220918.text: ...It's true. I've been investigating the prophecy for hundreds of years.

40220919.text: I once had informants all over Teyvat, searching for clues and feeding information back to me.

40220920.text: I've tried all kinds of ways, too, to hold back the sea. Anything to keep the coastline from advancing...

40220921.text: But all my efforts proved to be futile in the end. Really, the truth has been clear to me for a very long time...

40220922.text: We cannot make an enemy of the divine. No matter what we do, the will of the Heavenly Principles will have its way, and the prophecy shall be fulfilled...

40220201.text: Ladies and gentlemen... this concludes my opening performance.

40220202.text: Now, without further ado... we may proceed to the trial of our god.

40220203.text: Ah, so this is what it is. Yes... You deserve praise for the effort you took to raise the dramatic stakes.

40220204.text: Do not forget, however, that I am Focalors, the God of Justice — the embodiment of justice itself. Does it not strike you as even the least bit absurd to bring the very concept of justice to trial?

40220205.text: May I interpret these words... as your refusal to stand trial?

40220206.text: In that case, you will have the opportunity to defend your honor through a duel.

40220207.text: You... You would draw your blade against a god?

40220208.text: I see... It seems like you have made up your mind.

40220209.text: Paimon can't believe it... She... She just surrendered!?

40220211.text: What the heck is going on? Did I just see an Archon surrender to a human?

40220213.text: Lady Furina, what is the meaning of this?

40220215.text: It would seem that there has been a misunderstanding. To be clear, the raising of both hands is not always an indication of surrender...

40220217.text: ...I raised my hands just now to indicate my acceptance of the trial. No duel shall be necessary.

40220218.text: I will admit that I've been running away for a long time.

40220219.text: I'm sorry, everyone. I was unable to protect the people of Poisson... It is my duty to stand trial for my crimes.

40220220.text: You are not the only ones to be disappointed in me. I, too, am exceedingly disappointed in myself.

40220221.text: Whew... But now, it is time for the Hydro Archon to show you her courage and resolve!

40220222.text: I, Furina, will use this trial to show the world the true meaning of justice!

40220224.text: Applaud and rejoice! One of the most outrageous and fantastical arcs known to the Opera Epiclese is now unfolding before your eyes!

40220225.text: Mark my words — this shall be one of the most exhilarating and brilliant shows ever to grace the stage of Fontaine! The trial of the Hydro Archon, Focalors, will now begin!

40220229.text: Why does it feel like Furina just took over the whole thing... Like c'mon, didn't she just get forced to stand trial for her crimes?

40220230.text: Also, even though she's still acting super dramatic, she is taking this seriously this time, right?

40220231.text: Alright, then... Who will be my opponent in this trial?

40220232.text: The court asks the prosecutor to please take the stand.

40220234.text: Is that so... Very well. Then please speak, witness of Teyvat, my accuser and fated opponent.

40220235.text: (We were so close to getting her to tell us the truth... And it still turned out like this in the end.)

40220236.text: (It's okay, though. As long as we can defeat Furina in court, we'll still have a chance to figure everything out.)

40220237.text: Also, please allow me to ask, as the final question before the trial begins...

40220238.text: Just how much work did you do to force me onto this stage?

40220239.text: Well... We did do a lot of prep after the meeting that day...

40220240.text: I can go over the tasks assigned to the Spina di Rosula, since they were rather straightforward and easy.

40220241.text: Navia, the President of the Spina di Rosula...

40220242.text: Most of the people who participated in the disturbance this morning were my subordinates.

40220243.text: They changed into plain clothes, and came to the opera house as regular audience members, waiting for the perfect opportunity to incite insurrection against you.

40220244.text: The people's resentment against their Archon has been building as more and more of the prophecy is fulfilled. A spark was all we needed to turn smoldering anger into a flame.

40220245.text: Moreover, according to our understanding and analysis of you, when something like that occurred, you would likely flee the scene and head to Poisson by yourself.

40220246.text: So, we arranged for a second group to lie in wait there...

40220247.text: So, you mean... The ones who scoured the settlement for me were also from the Spina...

40220248.text: And their goal was to force you to step into the Giant Magic Box, so you may personally participate in the greatest magic performance in all of Fontainian history.

40220249.text: That's right. That house was a magic box, rather than someone's residence.

40220250.text: As the "Super Ultimate" version of the setup that I used when I first performed at the Opera Epiclese...

40220251.text: The volume of the box was increased by a whole order of magnitude, and the distance it traversed was the entire gap between Poisson and Erinnyes. Its cargo, of course...

40220252.text: ...Was an Archon, instead of a human.

40220253.text: My thanks, Furina. Without your help, we could never have pulled off such an extraordinary performance.

40220255.text: Of course, this performance was only made possible with "Father"'s support. The House of the Hearth spent a massive amount of labor and Mora to pull this off...

40220256.text: We had to select a location, construct the Giant Magic Box, dig a tunnel, and open up a path through the water... It was a lot of work for all of us.

40220257.text: So, in other words... the "earthquake" that we felt within the Giant Magic Box was just a normal tremor from the transportation of the whole house?

40220258.text: That's right. It wasn't a sign of another disaster to come.

40220261.text: Hmph, then... I can guess Neuvillette and Clorinde's parts.

40220262.text: You gathered a crowd, prepared a stage, and made sure that the Champion Duelist would be immediately ready for a fight...

40220263.text: All so that as soon as I appeared on the stage, the trial may commence without a hitch. Am I right?

40220265.text: Well, Clorinde, I must commend you for your courage. Only the most outstanding Champion Duelist in all of Fontaine would accept a duel with an Archon without flinching.

40220267.text: #As for you, {NICKNAME}... I suppose your role was to keep me distracted with conversation once you found me in Poisson.

40220268.text: You'd make sure that I didn't notice anything amiss, before revealing yourself as my prosecutor once we'd arrived onto the stage...

40221501.text: It has been established that all Fontainians can dissolve in water from the Primordial Sea. And that means...

40221502.text: Since you insist on claiming to be a god and not a human, then there's a method that you can use right here and now to eliminate all suspicions of you being the latter.

40221503.text: Miss Navia, please apply to serve as a temporary attorney for the prosecution before addressing the court. Though you act in partnership with the prosecutor, you must still adhere to proper procedure.

40221504.text: Super sorry, Monsieur Chief Justice. I swear this really will be the last time that I'll speak out of turn.

40221505.text: Now, I've brought some seawater from Poisson. As everyone knows, a massive flood struck the area not long ago, taking many lives...

40221506.text: ...Including those of some of my closest friends.

40221507.text: So, Miss Furina, would you dare to touch some of this seawater?

40221508.text: If we are to believe that you are indeed the real Hydro Archon, touching this seawater would have no effect on you. All it should do is strengthen your case.

40221509.text: But if you don't dare to touch it, then we would have basically proved the reverse.

40221510.text: Oh, and I must remind you that after the disaster at Poisson, nobody wants to see any more people dissolve.

40221511.text: I do hope you'll act prudently, and choose the simpler path of admitting guilt.

40221512.text: Navia from the Spina di Rosula... The Spina has governed Poisson for many years... I guess her suggestion is valid.

40221513.text: If Lady Furina is indeed just a human, she's probably a Fontainian like all the rest of us. Would she really dare to try...?

40221516.text: Lady Furina, this "test" has been unilaterally proposed by the prosecution. As it falls outside the realm of standard court proceedings, you possess the right to decline participation.

40221518.text: Well, of course he had to tell her that, but refusing to participate is basically the same as a confession of guilt.

40221519.text: She's just staring at the water without saying a single word... It really does seem like she's quite terrified of it. That could only mean...

40221520.text: (What's going on? Is she really planning to... That's not what we thought she would...)

40221522.text: Due to the inherent risk of the test, Lady Furina, you may—

40221528.text: I... I'm fine! Look! Look at me, everyone. My hand is still here. I haven't been dissolved!

40221529.text: Will you believe me now? I really am your Archon. I'm nothing like a normal human, who would fall apart as soon as they touch this water. Really, was this not the most obvious thing in the world?

40221530.text: Miss Sigewinne? If you are present, Miss Sigewinne, please come forward and attend to the defendant.

40221532.text: Don't be nervous, it'll just take a few seconds... Hmm, let me see...

40221534.text: Please announce the results of your evaluation to the court, Miss Sigewinne.

40221535.text: As everyone doubtlessly saw, Miss Furina was displaying symptoms of hyperventilation and flushed skin. These indicate that...

40221536.text: She was experiencing the adverse effects of exposure to Primordial Seawater. The extent to which she was affected is the same as other humans when exposed to Primordial Seawater of a similar concentration.

40221537.text: Thank you, Miss Sigewinne. Lady Furina, you may return to the defendant's stand.

40221538.text: Wait. What did she just say? I didn't get dissolved! Shouldn't that be enough to prove my innocence?

40221539.text: Well, considering your tendency to run from your problems, we did originally prepare a direct sample of the seawater around Poisson.

40221540.text: However, after extensive discussion, we exchanged it for a sample that is not concentrated enough to dissolve an actual human. After all, on the off chance that something entirely unexpected might occur...

40221541.text: We don't want anyone else to lose their life to the sea.

40221542.text: Yeah, so out of regard for Furina's life, you secured a low concentration sample, and asked the head nurse to serve as an expert witness...

40221543.text: It's a great thing that the direct sample wasn't actually used. Furina could have...

40221545.text: (But what's really going on here? Furina can't have not known the consequences of touching that water as a human...)

40221546.text: (This is too unlike how she usually acts... Unless... It's actually more important for her to keep up her facade than to save her own life!?)

40221547.text: (But... hadn't she given up on everything a long time ago?)

40221548.text: Listen to me, listen to me, everyone... Please don't give me such cold and disdainful looks. What happened just now didn't prove a single thing!

40221549.text: Think about it. How can you conclusively prove that an Archon can't also be affected by the Primordial Seawater?

40221550.text: Also, also! If I was really just a human, why would I dare to just put my hand in that kind of water!?

40221551.text: ...Please, everyone, anyone, just listen to me. I swear, I really am your Archon...

40221553.text: ...I don't think anything she says at this point will sway anyone. The odds are just too stacked against her now...

40221554.text: With all the things that have been said... Paimon doesn't think there's any way left for Furina to win.

40221555.text: I believe the time for argument and presentation of evidence has come to an end. If there are no objections, we will move on to the final judgment.

40221557.text: In my capacity as Chief Justice, I shall now render judgment on Furina's misrepresentation of herself as the Archon of Fontaine. As a human who knowingly deceived her fellow citizens, Furina is—

40221559.text: We shall now turn to the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale to render the final verdict on the charges.

40221560.text: According to the judgment of the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, Furina is—

40221562.text: Wh—What's wrong? What's the Oratrice's verdict?

40221565.text: ...No, the Oratrice also displays a guilty verdict.

40221567.text: However, the exact wording of the verdict is thus. "The Hydro Archon, guilty"...

40221568.text: "To be punished via the death sentence."

40221570.text: That's actually one of the available sentences!? I've always thought that it was just a myth...

40221571.text: The one and only time the death sentence has been handed out at the court, and it's been given to the very person we've worshipped as the God of Justice? What an unexpected twist...

40221573.text: Furina's been sentenced to death by the Oratrice!? We just wanted to use the trial to show her the seriousness of things, so she'd tell us the truth... How did things escalate this quickly!?

40221574.text: This outcome is indeed quite strange. According to Fontaine's current definitions of justice, as well as its recommendations for criminal sentences...

40221575.text: Is this sentence really appropriate for the crimes that have been committed...?

40221576.text: Yeah, even Vacher wasn't sentenced to death by the Oratrice... You know, the real evil mastermind behind the serial disappearances case.

40220401.text: Err... Excuse me... If I may interrupt...

40220403.text: Freminet! You finally made it. I assume this means you've completed your mission?

40220404.text: Mhm. Any mission "Father" assigns to me will always be top priority.

40220425.text: With some help from the other Fatui, Freminet brings a stone slate onto the stage...

40220405.text: Is that the first prophecy slate?

40220406.text: Huh, so The Knave privately arranged for Freminet to try and find the missing slate.

40220407.text: I looked everywhere, and finally found it at the bottom of the sea. It took me a long time to get around some dangerous stretches of water...

40220408.text: But... has the trial already concluded? Then... Doesn't that mean I've come too late? Oh no, "Father" will be disappointed in me...

40220411.text: Thank you for your hard work, Mr. Freminet. Please allow me to review the record left on the slate.

40220413.text: #{NICKNAME}, I believe that you have also already seen the other existing slates. I would like you to also come here and confirm their contents.

40220414.text: Huh... So what do you see? What is it?

subQuests.subQuestName: Discover the connection between the events in real life and the slates

40220601.text: Huh, oh, Paimon gets it now... So that's how you can make sense of it...

40220602.text: But then it feels like... We're going to have to share some truly shocking revelations.

40220606.text: Incredible. Lyney, did you hear that?

40220608.text: All Fontainians were originally created by the late previous Hydro Archon, with Oceanids as their basis.

40220609.text: The evidence for that can be found in... How only Fontainians could dissolve in Primordial Seawater, and how all the girls Vacher dissolved were also turned into Oceanids...

40220610.text: Oh, and according to Navia, when she was about to get dissolved, she also saw everyone gathered around for a trial, all of them in the shape of Oceanids...

subQuests.subQuestName: Find the source of the calamity in the prophecy slates

40220701.text: We didn't believe that such a crazy disaster could happen at first, did we? But after "that incident," it was just a question of "when," and not "if."

40220702.text: Indeed, that greedy beast in the Primordial Sea is the true root cause of the catastrophe.

subQuests.subQuestName: Discuss how to deal with the All-Devouring Narwhal

40220801.text: That was way too close! How did that thing just burst into the opera house!? Wait. Was that the huge whale you saw in your dream?

40220804.text: So, we've met it at last... I understand very well why it has chosen to make an appearance here.

40220805.text: That "whale" does not belong to Teyvat. It is a monster that has traversed the stars, weeping all the while.

40220806.text: It has been greedily consuming the energy from the planet's Primordial Sea, using it to grow. That is the main cause for the rising sea levels...

40220807.text: And once it has finished consuming all of the energy contained within the Sea, its next step will be...

40220808.text: You said that when the Hydro Archon first created Fontainians out of Oceanids, she filled their blood vessels with Primordial Seawater...

40220809.text: Precisely. That whale finds the "blood" of Fontainians nigh impossible to resist.

40220810.text: Therefore, when it left the Primordial Sea, it decided to make its next stop a packed opera house full of food — food in the form of Fontainians.

40220811.text: We just barely managed to push it back, right? In that case... Won't it come back to target the people again once it's managed to recover its strength?

40220812.text: That is correct. Indeed, it is more accurate to say that we should thank that Harbinger for buying us some time. Without him, the whale would have likely come onto land far sooner.

40220813.text: From the way he looked, he must have been fighting the creature for quite a long time.

40220814.text: That battle maniac... We've always known that he had a special connection with that whale, but we definitely didn't expect it to help us out like this.

40220815.text: Anyway, now that we know that this whale is the actual cause of the disaster recorded in the prophecy, all we need to do to stop the prophecy would be to find a way to beat it up, right?

40220818.text: It had already absorbed too much of the Primordial Sea's energy before we could notice it. At this point, it has become practically integrated with the Sea itself.

40220819.text: Even if the entirety of Teyvat were to be destroyed, it could still survive, and swim off towards some other world.

40220820.text: That... That's not something I will accept.

40220821.text: We've already done everything we can, and we even found the true culprit...

40220822.text: We've come so far! You can't just tell me that the last hurdle is some impossible foe. That's just not fair.

40220823.text: Indeed. That's not how a grand performance should end.

40220824.text: I'll fight it to the end. No matter what.

40220825.text: So the prophecy will be fulfilled no matter what, huh...

40220827.text: The prophecy... Yes, what has been prophesized will be fulfilled. You may view such things as "the history of the future."

40220828.text: (After everything, it still turned out like this... We couldn't fight against fate.)

40220829.text: (Wait, but if this is all about fate...)

40220830.text: Just as prophecies are usually only the future as seen from the perspectives of the gods, could things be happening in hidden corners where the gods' gaze does not fall?

40220831.text: Ultimately, fate shall serve as your only guide no matter what will happen in Teyvat's future. All you need to do is to play your part.

40220832.text: (Could it be... That even if the prophecy will be fulfilled, there will still be a way to save everyone?)

40220834.text: (Wait, I forgot about Furina! What was it that she wanted to say to me at that last moment, in the Giant Magic Box?)

40220301.text: The prosecution and the defense are both in position. The trial shall now begin.

40220302.text: Come on, Neuvillette. There's no need to repeat all the unimportant legalese.

40220303.text: Just fast forward to the part where the prosecution lays out my offenses. As the defendant, and the lead actress of this performance, I still haven't even been informed of my supposed guilt in all of this.

40220304.text: Of course, it is only natural for humans to struggle to understand the actions of a god. However, you will need more than that to convict me of a crime...

40220305.text: That is true, but my charge here is unrelated to your conduct as an Archon.

40220306.text: Instead, I would like to charge you as a fraud who's never been the Archon in the first place.

40220307.text: Wait... what was that? Lady Furina's a fraud?

40220308.text: Hey... I came here thinking that we were going to try the Hydro Archon for forsaking her duty, but did I hear that right? She's not our Archon at all?

40220310.text: Lady Furina. Do you plead guilty to the charge?

40220313.text: I plead not guilty. How can I be guilty?

40220314.text: There is no way that I, Focalors, otherwise known as Furina de Fontaine, a member of The Seven, and the Regina of All Waters, Kindreds, Peoples and Laws of Fontaine, could be anything other than your true Archon.

40220315.text: Yeah... Even though Lady Furina can be rather eccentric, isn't it going too far to doubt her very identity?

40220316.text: Yeah, I've never questioned her identity either. Sure, Lady Furina can be super irresponsible, but what grounds does that prosecutor have to make such a huge claim...

40220317.text: I have cause to believe that common sense will prevail in this case. Many of the members of the audience have known me as the Hydro Archon ever since they were born — there would be no fooling their memory.

40220318.text: See? Even the Oratrice has decided to show me its favor. Are you sure you want to commit to a charge that will never be upheld?

40220319.text: If you wish to drop the case, I can promise you, as the God of Justice, that you will not have to face trial for making a false accusation. We will treat everything that's happened as a dramatic spectacle, and move on with our lives. What do you say to that?

40220320.text: An argument with near-impossible odds, huh? We have to not only refute Furina's claims, but also overturn the long-held beliefs of the people...

40220323.text: Well, I tried to give you the chance to surrender. If you must persist, then let me ask: If you believe I'm not the Archon, then what manner of being do you think I am?

40220324.text: And if I was not the Archon, then how did I manage to live for over five hundred years?

40220325.text: (I've got to think carefully... What do we know to be "special" about Furina, exactly?)

40221101.text: First of all, you may be a member of another long-lived race, which would allow you to naturally possess an extended lifespan. And second of all, even if that wasn't the case, there could be other ways to extend your life...

40221103.text: Hmph... Who gave you that idea? Was it The Knave? You'd sink so low as to use a Harbinger's words against me?

40221106.text: A curse... I once thought it possible that the aura of an Archon might naturally resemble a type of curse.

40221107.text: But in light of this claim, perhaps what I sensed was not your divinity, but a curse after all?

40221201.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound right. Paimon doesn't think this clue can be used as compelling evidence to build our case...

40221301.text: You tried to reference the Oratrice, but weren't you as confused as all the rest of us when the Oratrice declared Childe to be guilty without any proof? Otherwise, you should have come up with a good explanation for that by now...

40221302.text: Didn't I make myself clear at the time? The decisions of the gods are naturally difficult for humans to comprehend. There is no need to provide an explanation...

40221303.text: Lady Furina, I believe a reminder of your current circumstances is in order.

40221304.text: While the court is in session, the principles of justice and the law must come before all else. While you are an Archon, you are also first and foremost the defendant in this trial.

40221305.text: You will prove yourself unable to defend against the prosecution's charges if you continue to withhold vital information against the rules of the court.

40221306.text: I never thought... You'd use that kind of rhetoric against me...

40221307.text: That was no trick of rhetoric, Lady Furina. I have merely reiterated the rules of the court, rules that all should respect and follow.

40221309.text: So, you neither knew why Childe was declared guilty, nor did you understand the structure and operations of the Oratrice...

40221310.text: Instead of having been created by you, the "manifestations of authority" you mentioned have been made by the real Hydro Archon, haven't they?

40221311.text: The real Hydro Archon? Well, now you're really losing me.

40221312.text: It is true that I did not know why the Oratrice gave out a guilty verdict that day.

40221313.text: But the Oratrice handed out that verdict unilaterally, and it has been operating independently ever since it was first created.

40221314.text: You can't... You can't argue that just because a divine creation is flawed, that the god behind it must also be no god at all.

40221315.text: She's still throwing out all kinds of excuses... Seems like she's confident that we won't be able to produce proof that she has no power over the Oratrice.

40221318.text: My power as an Archon? There are many ordinary citizens in the audience. How can I just carelessly demonstrate the formidable power of an Archon...

40221319.text: If that poses a concern, I'm prepared to extend my protection to the audience.

40221320.text: Erm... Y—You don't need to go that far...

40221401.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound right. Paimon doesn't think this clue can be used as compelling evidence to build our case...

40221601.text: Hmm, that doesn't sound right. Paimon doesn't think this clue can be used as compelling evidence to build our case...

40221701.text: We know from the case of the serial disappearances of young women that Fontainians can be dissolved in Primordial seawater...

40221703.text: Perhaps what is about to take place has all happened before.

40221704.text: It's not as simple as falling into the sea...

40221705.text: The prophecy from the stone slates found its way into society, but not many people believed it at first...

40221706.text: That doesn't sound quite right. Let's think about this some more...

40221710.text: They will dissolve into the waters of the Primordial Sea, and then they'll be like the Poisson residents Navia met when she fell into the sea... They'll turn into Oceanids.

40221711.text: The first stone slate describes what you had just said. It seems to show the previous Hydro Archon using her divine power, and then the Oceanids turn into humans...

40221717.text: Does that mean that Fontainians are transformed Oceanids? Paimon wasn't expecting that... But if Oceanids can turn into humans, then perhaps this process can be "reversed" as well?

40221712.text: The second stone slate shows Celestia floating in the sky, and the Hydro Archon and her people worshiping it together... but the heavens still brought judgment down upon them.

40221718.text: This must be the point when the Hydro Archon and the Fontainians were branded with their "original sin." Does this mean that the "original sin" and the "Hydro Archon's sin" are the same thing?

40221713.text: The third slate shows the Hydro Archon sinking into the sea, surrounded by many people.

40221719.text: Huh, that reminds Paimon, didn't we also watch that happen to someone else?

40221714.text: Well, the fourth slate is the prophecy the Fontainians have been talking about. People dissolving into the sea, the Hydro Archon crying on her throne, and so on.

40221720.text: We didn't believe that such a crazy disaster could happen at first, did we? But after "that incident," it was just a question of "when," and not "if."

40221715.text: It was both dream and reality.

40221721.text: The "Hydro Archon" was sentenced to death in court, shocking everyone present. Perhaps this means that her sin was actually Fontaine's "original sin"...

40221722.text: Navia fell into the water inside those ruins, and she nearly dissolved. She was surrounded by the people of Poisson in a court within her consciousness, and was forced to take part in a trial meant to make her stay.

40221723.text: The eruption of the Primordial Sea at the Fortress of Meropide was the surest sign that the prophecy was about to come to pass no matter what.

40221724.text: The stone slates' content can all be verified by recent events. If we combined what we know together, loads of truths should come to light...

40221725.text: And the first stone slate tells us that long ago, the Hydro Archon used her power to turn Oceanids into humans...

40221726.text: This might be the reason that Fontainians can dissolve...

40221727.text: The true "sin" of the Hydro Archon that Neuvillette mentioned...

40221728.text: And the "original sin" cast down on the people of Fontaine by Celestia, as recorded on the stone slates...

40221729.text: When Navia fell into the sea, her consciousness was subjected to judgment.

40221730.text: The stone slates show the people gathered around the Hydro Archon in the sea... Could that be alluding to the same thing?

40221731.text: The Fortress of Meropide was nearly flooded with Primordial Seawater, which we know can cause Fontainians to dissolve. It seems increasingly likely that the prophecy may come true.

40221732.text: If we hadn't dealt with it in time, things could have gone very badly.

40221733.text: They'll dissolve into the Primordial Sea, but won't cease to exist... Their essence will flow in the seawater, converge... and take the form of an Oceanid.

40221802.text: The truth, the original sin, the trial... and the root cause of the disaster.

40221810.text: If we're talking about a "true culprit," that could only be "that thing" inside the Primordial Sea, right?

40221814.text: This eruption was just a small warning of the things to come. We must find the root cause of the disaster...

40229901.text: This place looks deserted... Guess all the survivors must have evacuated already. All that's left here are signs of devastation...

40229902.text: Could Furina really be here? Let's try to find her as soon as possible.
